description:
The Sanitary Napkin Scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to promote menstrual hygiene among women and girls across the country. 

This scheme was officially launched on 1st January 2011. 

It was introduced under the National Health Mission. 

The primary objective of the Sanitary Napkin Scheme is to provide affordable sanitary napkins to women and adolescent girls. 

The scheme aims to ensure that menstrual hygiene products are accessible to all, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. 

The initiative is designed to combat the stigma associated with menstruation and to promote awareness about menstrual health. 

The scheme targets the reduction of health risks associated with poor menstrual hygiene. 

According to the National Family Health Survey 2015-16, only 57.6% of women in India use hygienic methods of menstrual protection. 

The Sanitary Napkin Scheme aims to increase this percentage significantly. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to provide sanitary napkins at a subsidized rate. 

The government aims to make sanitary napkins available at a cost of INR 6 per pack. 

Each pack contains six sanitary napkins. 

This pricing is aimed at making the product affordable for low-income families. 

The scheme also includes the establishment of production units for sanitary napkins. 

These units are often set up as self-help groups or cooperatives. 

This approach not only provides sanitary napkins but also creates employment opportunities for women. 

The scheme encourages local production to reduce costs and increase availability. 

In terms of benefits, the scheme provides free sanitary napkins to girls in schools. 

The initiative also includes awareness programs about menstrual hygiene management. 

The government has set a target to reach at least 1.5 crore women and girls annually through this scheme. 

Eligibility for the scheme primarily includes women and adolescent girls aged between 10 to 49 years. 

There are no specific income criteria for eligibility. 

However, the scheme focuses on reaching out to those from economically weaker sections. 

The application process for the Sanitary Napkin Scheme is relatively straightforward. 

Women and girls can access sanitary napkins through local health centers or schools. 

In many cases, the distribution is handled by Anganwadi workers. 

These workers play a crucial role in disseminating information and distributing sanitary napkins. 

Required documents for accessing the scheme are minimal. 

Typically, no formal documentation is required to receive sanitary napkins. 

However, beneficiaries may need to provide basic identification details. 

The timeline for the distribution of sanitary napkins is ongoing. 

The government ensures that sanitary napkins are available throughout the year. 

Disbursement schedules may vary based on local needs and availability. 

The implementing authority for the Sanitary Napkin Scheme is the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 

The National Health Mission oversees the execution of the scheme at the state level. 

State health departments are responsible for the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Contact details for the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare can be found on their official website. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders. 

Many NGOs and women's groups have supported the initiative. 

They have highlighted the importance of menstrual hygiene in improving women's health. 

The scheme has also contributed to reducing school drop-out rates among girls. 

Many girls miss school during their menstrual periods due to a lack of sanitary products. 

By providing access to sanitary napkins, the scheme aims to keep girls in school. 

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to educate communities about menstruation. 

These campaigns focus on breaking the taboo surrounding menstruation. 

They encourage open discussions about menstrual health. 

The Sanitary Napkin Scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve women's health in India. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 3, which aims to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all. 

The scheme has been instrumental in reducing the health risks associated with poor menstrual hygiene. 

It has also contributed to the empowerment of women by promoting their health and hygiene. 

The government has allocated significant funds to support the Sanitary Napkin Scheme. 

In the Union Budget for 2021-22, the government allocated INR 1,000 crore for the National Health Mission. 

A portion of this budget is specifically designated for menstrual hygiene management initiatives. 

The scheme has also been recognized internationally for its impact on women's health. 

Various studies have shown that access to sanitary napkins leads to improved health outcomes for women. 

The Sanitary Napkin Scheme is a crucial step towards achieving gender equality in health. 

It addresses a fundamental need for women and girls across the country. 

The initiative not only provides products but also fosters a supportive environment for discussing menstrual health. 

Overall, the Sanitary Napkin Scheme represents a comprehensive approach to menstrual hygiene management in India. 

It combines product availability with education and awareness to create a holistic solution. 

The scheme continues to evolve based on feedback and changing needs. 

It remains a vital part of the government's efforts to improve women's health and well-being. 

The Sanitary Napkin Scheme is a testament to the commitment of the Indian government to address women's health issues. 

It serves as a model for similar initiatives in other countries. 

By focusing on accessibility and education, the scheme aims to create a healthier future for women and girls in India. 

The impact of the Sanitary Napkin Scheme is expected to grow as awareness increases and more women gain access to these essential products. 

The government remains dedicated to ensuring that menstrual hygiene is a priority in public health discussions. 

This initiative is a critical component of the larger agenda for women's empowerment in India. 

The Sanitary Napkin Scheme is a significant stride towards a healthier and more equitable society.
